stem.text: Which of the following statements describe a valid test objective?

options.text: To prove that there are no unfixed defects in the system under test
options.rationale: Is not correct. It is impossible to prove that there are no defects anymore in the system under test. See testing principle 1

options.text: To prove that there will be no failures after the implementation of the system into production
options.rationale: Is not correct. See testing principle 7

options.text: To reduce the risk level of the test object and to build confidence in the quality level
options.rationale: Is correct. Testing finds defects and failures which reduces the level of risk and at the same time gives more confidence in the quality level of the test object

options.text: To verify that there are no untested combinations of inputs
options.rationale: Is not correct. It is impossible to test all combinations of inputs (see testing principle 2)

stem.text: Which of the following options shows an example of test activities that contribute to success?

options.text: Having testers involved during various software development lifecycle (SDLC) activities will help to detect defects in work products
options.rationale: Is correct. It is important that testers are involved from the beginning of the software development lifecycle (SDLC). It will increase understanding of design decisions and will detect defects early.

options.text: Testers try not to disturb the developers while coding, so that the developers write better code
options.rationale: Is not correct. Both developers and testers will have more understanding of each other's work products and how to test the code

options.text: Testers collaborating with end users help to improve the quality of defect reports during component integration and system testing
options.rationale: Is not correct. End users will not help the testers in increasing the quality of defect reports; also, users usually do not participate in low-level testing levels like integration testing

options.text: Certified testers will design much better test cases than non-certified testers
options.rationale: Is not correct. Being certified does not automatically mean that the tester will be better in test design

stem.text: You have been assigned as a tester to a team producing a new system incrementally. You have noticed that no changes have been made to the existing regression test cases for several iterations and no new regression defects were identified. Your manager is happy, but you are not. Which testing principle explains your skepticism?

options.text: Tests wear out
options.rationale: Is correct. This principle means that if the same tests are repeated over and over again, eventually these tests no longer find any new defects. This is probably why the tests all passed in this release as well

options.text: Absence-of-defects fallacy
options.rationale: Is not correct. This principle says about the mistaken belief that just finding and fixing a large number of defects will ensure the success of a system

options.text: Defects cluster together
options.rationale: Is not correct. This principle says that a small number of components usually contain most of the defects

options.text: Exhaustive testing is impossible
options.rationale: Is not correct. This principle states that testing all combinations of inputs and preconditions is not feasible

stem.text: You work in a team that develops a mobile application for food ordering. In the current iteration the team decided to implement the payment functionality.
Which of the following activities is a part of test analysis?

options.text: Estimating that testing the integration with the payment service will take 8 person-days
options.rationale: Is not correct. Estimating the test effort is part of test planning

options.text: Deciding that the team should test if it is possible to properly share payment between many users
options.rationale: Is correct. This is an example of defining test conditions which is a part of test analysis

options.text: Using boundary value analysis (BVA) to derive the test data for the test cases that check the correct payment processing for the minimum allowed amount to be paid
options.rationale: Is not correct. Using test techniques to derive coverage items is a part of test design

options.text: Analyzing the discrepancy between the actual result and expected result after executing a test case that checks the process of payment with a credit card, and reporting a defect
options.rationale: Is not correct. Reporting defects found during dynamic testing is a part of test execution

The test environment has no significant influence on the test approach Thus:

stem.text: Which TWO of the following tasks belong MAINLY to a testing role?

options.text: Configure test environments
options.rationale: Is correct. This is done by the testers

options.text: Maintain the product backlog
options.rationale: Is not correct. The product backlog is built and maintained by the product owner

options.text: Design solutions to new requirements
options.rationale: Is not correct. This is done by the development team

options.text: Create the test plan
options.rationale: Is not correct. This is a managerial role

options.text: Analyze the test basis
options.rationale: Is correct. This is done by the testers since its technical task done as part of a test analysis.

stem.text: Which of the following skills (i-v) are the MOST important skills of a tester?

lines: iii.       Being a good team player
iv.        Planning and organizing the work of the team

options.text: ii and iv are important
options.rationale: Is not correct

options.text: i, iii and v are important
options.rationale: Is correct

options.text: i, ii and v are important
options.rationale: Is not correct

options.text: iii and iv are important
options.rationale: Is not correct

questions.explanation: i. Is true. Having domain knowledge is an important tester skill ii. Is false. This is a task of the business analyst together with the business representative iii. Is true. Being a good team player is an important skill iv. Is false. Planning and organizing the work of the team is a task of the test manager or, mostly in an Agile software development project, the whole team and not just the tester v. Is true. Critical thinking is one of the most important skills of testers Thus:

stem.text: How is the whole team approach present in the interactions between testers and business representatives?

options.text: Business representatives decide on test automation approaches
options.rationale: Is not correct. The test automation approach is defined by testers with the help of developers and business representatives

options.text: Testers help business representatives to define a test strategy
options.rationale: Is not correct. The test strategy is decided in collaboration with the developers

options.text: Business representatives are not part of the whole team approach
options.rationale: Is not correct. Testers, developers, and business representatives are part of the whole team approach

options.text: Testers help business representatives to create suitable acceptance tests
options.rationale: Is correct. Testers will work closely with business representatives to ensure that the desired quality levels are achieved. This includes supporting and collaborating with them to help them create suitable acceptance tests

stem.text: Consider the following rule: “for every SDLC activity there is a corresponding test activity”. In which SDLC models does this rule hold?

options.text: Only in sequential development models
options.rationale: Is not correct

options.text: Only in iterative development models
options.rationale: Is not correct

options.text: Only in iterative and incremental development models
options.rationale: Is not correct

options.text: In sequential, incremental, and iterative development models
options.rationale: Is correct. This rule holds for all SDLC models

stem.text: Which of the following statements BEST describes the acceptance test-driven development (ATDD) approach?

options.text: In ATDD, acceptance criteria are typically created based on the given/when/then format
options.rationale: Is not correct. It is more often used in behavior-driven development (BDD)

options.text: In ATDD, test cases are mainly created at component testing and are code-oriented
options.rationale: Is not correct. It is the description of test-driven development (TDD)

options.text: In ATDD, tests are created, based on acceptance criteria to drive the development of the related software
options.rationale: Is correct. In acceptance test-driven development (ATDD) tests are written from acceptance criteria as part of the design process

options.text: in ATDD, tests are based on the desired behavior of the software, which makes it easier for team members to understand them
options.rationale: Is not correct. It is used in BDD

stem.text: Which of the following is NOT an example of the shift-left approach?

options.text: Reviewing the user requirements before they are formally accepted by the stakeholders
options.rationale: Is not correct. Early review is an example of the shift-left approach

options.text: Writing a component test before the corresponding code is written
options.rationale: Is not correct. TDD is an example of the shift-left approach

options.text: Executing a performance efficiency test for a component during component testing
options.rationale: Is not correct. Early non-functional testing is an example of the shift-left approach

options.text: Writing a test script before setting up the configuration management process
options.rationale: Is correct. Test scripts should be subject to configuration management, so it makes no sense to create the test scripts before this process is set up

stem.text: Which of the arguments below would you use to convince your manager to organize retrospectives at the end of each release cycle?

options.text: Retrospectives are very popular these days and clients would appreciate it if we added them to our processes
options.rationale: Is not correct. Retrospectives are more useful for identifying improvement opportunities and have little importance for clients

options.text: Organizing retrospectives will save the organization money because without them end user representatives do not provide immediate feedback about the product
options.rationale: Is not correct. Retrospectives are not aimed to collect feedback about the product, but about the process. Additionally, retrospectives are internal activity for the team and should not include end user representatives

options.text: Process weaknesses identified during the retrospective can be analyzed and serve as a to do list for the organization’s continuous process improvement program
options.rationale: Is correct. Regularly conducted retrospectives, when appropriate follow up activities occur, are critical to continual improvement of development and testing

options.text: Retrospectives embrace five values including courage and respect, which are crucial to maintain continuous improvement in the organization
options.rationale: Is not correct. Courage and respect are values of Extreme Programming and are not closely related to retrospectives

Tests are repeated once you are informed that all defects found in the test run are corrected and a new version of the software is available. Which of the above tests are executed as regression tests?

options.rationale: Is not correct

options.text: Only 5, 7
options.rationale: Is correct
Is not correct

options.text: Only 5, 6
options.rationale: Is not correct

questions.explanation: Because TC1 and TC3 failed in Execution 1 (i.e., test (1) and test (3)), test (4) and test (6) are confirmation tests. Because TC2 and TC3 failed in Execution 2 (i.e., tests (5) and (6)), test (8) and test (9) are also confirmation tests. TC2 passed in Execution 1 (i.e., test (2)), so test (5) is a regression test. TC1 passed in the Execution 2 (i.e., test (4)), so test (7) is also a regression test. Thus:

stem.text: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of static testing?

options.text: Having less expensive defect management due to the ease of detecting defects later in the SDLC
options.rationale: Is correct. Defect management is no less expensive. Finding and fixing defects later in the SDLC is more costly

options.text: Fixing defects found during static testing is generally much less expensive than fixing defects found during dynamic testing
options.rationale: Is not correct. This is a benefit of static testing

options.text: Finding coding defects that might not have been found by only performing dynamic testing
options.rationale: Is not correct. This is a benefit of static testing

options.text: Detecting gaps and inconsistencies in requirements
options.rationale: Is not correct. This is a benefit of static testing

stem.text: Which of the following is a benefit of early and frequent feedback?

options.text: It improves the test process for future projects
options.rationale: Is not correct. Feedback can improve the test process, but if one only wants to improve future projects, the feedback does not need to come early or frequently

options.text: It forces customers to prioritize their requirements based on agreed risks
options.rationale: Is not correct. Feedback is not used to prioritize requirements

options.text: It provides a measure for the quality of changes
options.rationale: Is not correct. There is no one, recommended way to measure quality of changes. Also, this is not one of the benefits of early feedback that are mentioned in section 3.2.1

options.text: It helps avoid requirements misunderstandings
options.rationale: Is correct. Early and frequent feedback can prevent misunderstandings about requirements

stem.text: The reviews being used in your organization have the following attributes:

items: There is the role of a scribe
The main purpose is to evaluate quality
The meeting is led by the author of the work product
There is individual preparation
A review report is produced

stem.text: Which of the following review types is MOST likely being used?

options.text: Informal review
options.rationale: Is not correct

options.text: Walkthrough
options.rationale: Is correct

options.text: Technical review
options.rationale: Is not correct

options.text: Inspection
options.rationale: Is not correct

questions.explanation: Considering the attributes: • Specified for walkthroughs, technical reviews, and inspections; thus, the reviews being performed cannot be informal reviews • The purpose of evaluating quality is one of the most important objectives of a walkthrough • This is not allowed for inspections and is typically not done in technical reviews. A moderator is needed in walkthroughs and is allowed for informal reviews • All types of reviews can include individual preparation (even informal reviews) • All types of reviews can produce a review report, although informal reviews do not require documentation Thus:

stem.text: Which of these statements is NOT a factor that contributes to successful reviews?

options.text: Participants should dedicate adequate time for the review
options.rationale: Is not correct. Adequate time for individuals is a success factor

options.text: Splitting large work products into small parts to make the required effort less intense
options.rationale: Is not correct. Splitting work products into small adequate parts is a success factor

options.text: Participants should avoid behaviors that might indicate boredom, exasperation, or hostility to other participants
options.rationale: Is not correct. Avoiding behaviors that might indicate boredom, exasperation, etc. is a success factor

options.text: Failures found should be acknowledged, appreciated, and handled objectively
options.rationale: Is correct. During reviews one can find defects, not failures

stem.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of experience-based test techniques?

options.text: Test cases are created based on detailed design information
options.rationale: Is not correct. This is a common characteristic of white-box test techniques. Test conditions, test cases, and test data are derived from a test basis that may include code, software architecture, detailed design, or any other source of information regarding the structure of the software.

options.text: Items tested within the interface code section are used to measure coverage
options.rationale: Is not correct. This is a common characteristic of white-box test techniques. Coverage is measured based on the items tested within a selected structure and the test technique applied to the test basis

options.text: The test techniques heavily rely on the tester’s knowledge of the software and the business domain
options.rationale: Is correct. This is a common characteristic of experience-based test techniques. This knowledge and experience include expected use of the software, its environment, likely defects, and the distribution of those defects is used to define tests

options.text: The test cases are used to identify deviations from the requirements
options.rationale: Is not correct. This is a common characteristic of black-box test techniques. Test cases may be used to detect gaps within requirements and the implementation of the requirements, as well as deviations from the requirements

stem.text: You are testing a simplified apartment search form which has only two search criteria:

items: floor (with three possible options: ground floor; first floor; second or higher floor)
garden type (with three possible options: no garden; small garden; large garden)

stem.text: Each of the apartment on the ground floor has a garden, apartments on higher floors don’t. The form has a built-in validation mechanism that will not allow you to use the search criteria which violate this rule.
Each test has two input values: floor and garden type. You want to apply equivalence partitioning (EP) to cover each floor and each garden type in your tests.
What is the minimal number of test cases to achieve 100% EP coverage for valid partitions?

options.rationale: Is not correct
Is correct
Is not correct
Is not correct

questions.explanation: The situation presented in the question is described in the syllabus as “each choice” coverage. “Small garden” and “large garden” can go only with “ground floor”, so we need two test cases with “ground floor” which cover these two “garden type” partitions. We need two more test cases to cover the two other “floor” partitions. The remaining ”garden type” partition of “no garden” is covered by these tests. We need a total of four test cases: TC1 (ground floor, small garden) TC2 (ground floor, large garden) TC3 (first floor, no garden) TC4 (second or higher floor, no garden) Thus:

The final grade is assigned based on the final result, according to the following rules:

items: 0 – 50 points: failed

options.rationale: Is correct

stem.text: Your favorite bicycle daily rental store has just introduced a new Customer Relationship Management system and asked you, one of their most loyal members, to test it.
The implemented features are as follows:

items: Anyone can rent a bicycle, but members receive a 20% discount
However, if the return deadline is missed, the discount is no longer available
After 15 rentals, members get a gift: a T-Shirt

stem.text: Decision table describing the implemented features looks as follows:

lines: Conditions                   R1   R2    R3   R4   R5   R6   R7    R8
Being a member              T    T     T    T    F    F    F     F
Missed deadline             T    F     T    F    T    F    F     T
15th rental            F    F     T    T    F    F    T     T

stem.text: Actions
Based ONLY on the feature description of the Customer Relationship Management system, which of the above rules describes an impossible situation?

options.text: R4
options.rationale: Is not correct. A member without a missed deadline can get a discount and a gift T-Shirt after 15 bicycle rentals

options.text: R2
options.rationale: Is not correct. A member without a missed deadline can get a discount but no gift T-Shirt until they rented a bicycle 15 times

options.text: R6
options.rationale: Is not correct. Non-members cannot get a discount, even if they did not miss a deadline yet

options.text: R8
options.rationale: Is correct. No discount as a non-member that has also missed a deadline, but only members can receive a gift T-Shirt. Hence, the action is not correct

stem.text: You test a system whose lifecycle is modeled by the state transition diagram shown below. The system starts in the INIT state and ends its operation in the OFF state.
What is the MINIMAL number of test cases to achieve valid transitions coverage?

options.rationale: Is not correct
Is not correct
Is not correct
Is correct

questions.explanation: “test” and “error” transitions cannot occur in one test case. Neither can both “done” transitions. This means we need at least three test cases to achieve transition coverage. For example: TC1: test, done TC2: run, error, done TC3: run, pause, resume, pause, done Thus:

stem.text: Your test suite achieved 100% statement coverage. What is the consequence of this fact?

options.text: Each instruction in the code that contains a defect has been executed at least once
options.rationale: Is correct. Since 100% statement coverage is achieved, every statement, including the ones with defects, must have been executed and evaluated at least once

options.text: Any test suite containing more test cases than your test suite will also achieve 100% statement coverage
options.rationale: Is not correct. Coverage depends on what is tested, not on the number of test cases. For example, for code “if (x==0) y=1”, one test case (x=0) achieves 100% statement coverage, but two test cases (x=1) and (x=2) together achieve only 50% statement coverage

options.text: Each path in the code has been executed at least once
options.rationale: Is not correct. If there is a loop in the code there may be an infinite number of possible paths, so it is not possible to execute all the possible paths in the code

options.text: Every combination of input values has been tested at least once
options.rationale: Is not correct. Exhaustive testing is not possible (see the seven testing principles section in the syllabus). For example, for code “input x; print x” any single test with arbitrary x achieves 100% statement coverage, but covers one input value

stem.text: Which of the following is NOT true for white-box testing?

options.text: During white-box testing the entire software implementation is considered
options.rationale: Is not correct. The fundamental strength of white-box test techniques is that the entire software implementation is taken into account during testing

options.text: White-box coverage metrics can help identify additional tests to increase code coverage
options.rationale: Is not correct. White-box coverage measures provide an objective measure of coverage and provide the necessary information to allow additional tests to be generated to increase this coverage

options.text: White-box test techniques can be used in static testing
options.rationale: Is not correct. White-box test techniques can be used to perform reviews (static testing)

options.text: White-box testing can help identify gaps in requirements implementation
options.rationale: Is correct. This is the weakness of the white-box test techniques. They are not able to identify the missing implementation, because they are based solely on the test object structure, not on the requirements specification

stem.text: Which of the following BEST describes the concept behind error guessing?

options.text: Error guessing involves using your knowledge and experience of defects found in the past and typical errors made by developers
options.rationale: Is correct. The basic concept behind error guessing is that the tester tries to guess what errors may have been made by the developer and what defects may be in the test object based on past experience (and sometimes checklists)

options.text: Error guessing involves using your personal experience of development and the errors you made as a developer
options.rationale: Is not correct. Although a tester who used to be a developer may use their personal experience to help them when performing error guessing, the test technique is not based on prior knowledge of development

options.text: Error guessing requires you to imagine that you are the user of the test object and to guess errors the user could make interacting with it
options.rationale: Is not correct. Error guessing is not a usability technique for guessing how users may fail to interact with the test object

options.text: Error guessing requires you to rapidly duplicate the development task to identify the sort of errors a developer might make
options.rationale: Is not correct. Duplicating the development task has several flaws that make it impractical, such as the tester having equivalent skills to the developer and the time involved to perform the development. It is not error guessing

stem.text: In your project there has been a delay in the release of a brand-new application and test execution started late, but you have very detailed domain knowledge and good analytical skills. The full list of requirements has not yet been shared with the team, but management is asking for some test results to be presented.
Which test technique fits BEST in this situation?

options.text: Checklist-based testing
options.rationale: Is not correct. This is a new product. You probably do not have a checklist yet and test conditions might not be known due to missing requirements

options.text: Error guessing
options.rationale: Is not correct. This is a new product. You probably do not have enough information to make correct error guesses

options.text: Exploratory testing
options.rationale: Is correct. Exploratory testing is most useful when there are few known specifications and/or there is a pressing timeline for testing

options.text: Branch testing
options.rationale: Is not correct. Branch testing is time-consuming, and your management is asking about some test results now. Also, branch testing does not involve domain knowledge

stem.text: Which of the following BEST describes the way acceptance criteria can be documented?

options.text: Performing retrospectives to determine the actual needs of the stakeholders regarding a given user story
options.rationale: Is not correct. Retrospectives are used to capture lessons learned and to improve the development and testing process, not to document the acceptance criteria

options.text: Using the given/when/then format to describe an example test condition related to a given user story
options.rationale: Is correct. This is the standard way to document acceptance criteria

options.text: Using verbal communication to reduce the risk of misunderstanding the acceptance criteria by others
options.rationale: Is not correct. Verbal communication does not allow to physically document the acceptance criteria as part of a user story (”card” aspect in the 3C’s model)

options.text: Documenting risks related to a given user story in a test plan to facilitate the risk-based testing of a given user story
options.rationale: Is not correct. Acceptance criteria are related to a user story, not a test plan. Also, acceptance criteria are the conditions that have to be fulfilled to decide if the user story is complete. Risks are not such conditions

stem.text: Consider the following user story:
As an Editor I want to review content before it is published so that I can ensure the grammar is correct
and its acceptance criteria:

items: The user can log in to the content management system with "Editor" role
The editor can view existing content pages
The editor can edit the page content
The editor can add markup comments
The editor can save changes
The editor can reassign to the "content owner" role to make updates

stem.text: Which of the following is the BEST example of an ATDD test for this user story?

options.text: Test if the editor can save the document after edit the page content
options.rationale: Is correct. This test covers two acceptance criteria: one about editing the document and one about saving changes

options.text: Test if the content owner can log in and make updates to the content
options.rationale: Is not correct. Acceptance criteria cover the editor activities, not the content owner activities

options.text: Test if the editor can schedule the edited content for publication
options.rationale: Is not correct. Scheduling the edited content for publication may be a nice feature, but it is not covered by the acceptance criteria

options.text: Test if the editor can reassign to another editor to make updates
options.rationale: Is not correct. Acceptance criteria state about reassigning from an editor to the content owner, not to another editor

stem.text: How do testers add value to iteration and release planning?

options.text: Testers determine the priority of the user stories to be developed
options.rationale: Is not correct. Priorities for user stories are determined by the business representative together with the development team

options.text: Testers focus only on the functional aspects of the system to be tested
options.rationale: Is not correct. Testers focus on both functional and non-functional aspects of the system to be tested

options.text: Testers participate in the detailed risk identification and risk assessment of user stories
options.rationale: Is correct. According to the syllabus, this is one of the ways testers add value to iteration and release planning

options.text: Testers guarantee the release of high-quality software through early test design during the release planning
options.rationale: Is not correct. Early test design is not part of release planning. Early test design does not automatically guarantee the release of quality software

stem.text: Which TWO of the following options are the exit criteria for testing a system?

options.text: Test environment readiness
options.rationale: Is not correct. Test environment readiness is a resource availability criterion; hence it belongs to the entry criteria

options.text: The ability to log in to the test object by the tester
options.rationale: Is not correct. This is a resource availability criterion; hence it belongs to the entry criteria

options.text: Estimated defect density is reached
options.rationale: Is correct. Estimated defect density is a measure of diligence; hence it belongs to the exit criteria.

options.text: Requirements are translated into given/when/then format
options.rationale: Is not correct. Requirements translated into a given format result in testable requirements; hence it belongs to the entry criteria

options.text: Regression tests are automated
options.rationale: Is correct. Automation of regression tests is a completion criterion; hence it belongs to the exit criteria

stem.text: Your team uses the three-point estimation technique to estimate the test effort for a new high-risk feature. The following estimates were made:

items: Most optimistic estimation: 2 person-hours
Most likely estimation: 11 person-hours
Most pessimistic estimation: 14 person-hours

stem.text: What is the final estimate?

options.text: 9 person-hours
options.rationale: Is not correct

options.text: 14 person-hours
options.rationale: Is not correct

options.text: 11 person-hours
options.rationale: Is not correct

options.text: 10 person-hours
options.rationale: Is correct

questions.explanation: In the three-point estimation technique: E = (optimistic + 4*most likely + pessimistic)/6 E = (2+(4*11)+14)/6 = 10 Thus:

stem.text: Which test activity does a data preparation tool support?

options.text: Test monitoring and test control
options.rationale: Is not correct. Test monitoring involves the ongoing checking of all activities and comparison of actual progress against the test plan. options.text: Test analysis
options.rationale: Is not correct. Test analysis includes analysis of the test basis to identify test conditions and prioritize them. Test data are not prepared during this activity.

options.text: Test design and test implementation
options.rationale: Is correct. Test design and implementation can both include the identification, creation or acquisition of the testware necessary for test execution (e.g., test data).

options.text: Test completion
options.rationale: Is not correct. Test completion activities occur at project milestones (e.g., release, end of iteration, test level completion), so it is too late for preparing test data.

stem.text: Which of the following BEST explains a benefit of independence of testing?

options.text: The use of an independent test team allows project management to assign responsibility for the quality of the final deliverable to the test team
options.rationale: Is not correct. Quality should be the responsibility of everyone working on the project and not the sole responsibility of the test team

options.text: If a test team external to the organization can be afforded, then there are distinct benefits in terms of this external team not being so easily swayed by the delivery concerns of project management and the need to meet strict delivery deadlines
options.rationale: Is not correct. First, it is not a benefit if an external test team does not meet delivery deadlines, and second, there is no reason to believe that external test teams will feel they do not have to meet strict delivery deadlines

options.text: An independent test team can work separately from the developers, need not be distracted with project requirement changes, and can restrict communication with the developers to defect reporting through the defect management system
options.rationale: Is not correct. It is bad practice for the test team to work in complete isolation, and we would expect an external test team to be concerned with changing project requirements and communicating well with developers

options.text: When specifications contain ambiguities and inconsistencies, assumptions are made on their interpretation, and an independent tester can be useful in questioning those assumptions and the interpretation made by the developer
options.rationale: Is correct. Specifications are never perfect, meaning that assumptions will have to be made by the developer. An independent tester is useful in that they can challenge and verify the assumptions and subsequent interpretation made by the developer

stem.text: You are working as a tester in the team that follows the V-model. Which of the following activities CAN be performed in the initial phases of the SDLC?

options.text: Dynamic test execution
options.rationale: Is not correct. The executable code is usually created in the later phases, so dynamic test execution cannot be performed early in the SDLC

options.text: Static testing
options.rationale: Is correct. In sequential development models, in the initial phases, testers participate in requirement reviews, which is a form of static testing.

options.text: Test planning
options.rationale: Is correct. Test planning could be performed early in the SDLC before the test project begins together with test analysis and test design.

options.text: Acceptance test execution
options.rationale: Is not correct. Acceptance test execution can be performed when there is a working product. In sequential SDLC models the working product is usually delivered later in the SDLC

options.text: Maintenance testing
options.rationale: Is not correct. Maintenance testing when there is a working and deployed product, which is not done in the early phases of any SDLC.

stem.text: You work as a tester on a project on a mobile application for food ordering for one of your clients. The client sent you a list of requirements. One of them, with high priority, says

What test type did you perform?

options.text: Functional, because the test cases cover the user’s business requirement for the system
options.rationale: Is not correct. The fact that the requirement about the system’s performance comes directly from the client and that the performance is important from the business point of view (i.e., high priority) does not make these tests functional, because they do not check “what” the system does, but “how” (i.e., how fast the orders are processed)

options.text: Non-functional, because they measure the system’s performance
options.rationale: Is correct. This is an example of testing for performance efficiency, a type of non-functional testing

options.text: Functional, because the test cases interact with the user interface
options.rationale: Is not correct. From the scenario, we do not know if interacting with the user interface is a part of the test conditions. But even if we did, the main test objective of these tests is to check the performance, not the usability

options.text: White-box, because we need to know the internal structure of the program to measure the order processing time
options.rationale: Is not correct. We do not need to know the internal structure of the code to perform the performance efficiency testing. One can execute performance efficiency tests without structural knowledge

stem.text: Your organization’s test strategy suggests that once a system is going to be retired, data migration shall be tested. As part of what test type is this testing MOST likely to be performed?

options.rationale: Is correct. When a system is retired, this can require testing of data migration, which is a form of maintenance testing

options.text: Regression testing
options.rationale: Is not correct. Regression testing verifies whether a fix accidentally affected the behavior of other parts of the code, but now we are talking about data migration to a new system

options.text: Reliability testing
options.rationale: Is not correct. Portability testing focuses on transferring the system to another environment

options.text: Integration testing
options.rationale: Is not correct. Integration testing focuses on interactions between components and/or systems, not on data migration. Also, it is not a test type, but a test level.

stem.text: Which of the following statements about branch testing is CORRECT?

options.text: If a program includes only unconditional branches, then 100% branch coverage can be achieved without executing any test cases
options.rationale: Is not correct. In this case one test case is still needed since there is at least one (unconditional) branch to be covered

options.text: If the test cases exercise all unconditional branches in the code, then 100% branch coverage is achieved
options.rationale: Is not correct. Covering only unconditional branches does not imply covering all conditional branches

options.text: If 100% statement coverage is achieved, then 100% branch coverage is also achieved
options.rationale: Is not correct. 100% branch coverage implies 100% statement coverage, not otherwise. For example, for an IF decision without the ELSE, one test is enough to achieve 100% statement coverage, but it only achieves 50% branch coverage

options.text: If 100% branch coverage is achieved, then all decision outcomes in each decision statement in the code are exercised
options.rationale: Is correct. Each decision outcome corresponds to a conditional branch, so 100% branch coverage implies 100% coverage of the decision outcomes

options.text: Number of executed test procedures
options.rationale: Is not correct. The number of test cases executed does not tell us anything about the quality; test results might do

options.text: Number of defects found divided by the size of a work product
options.rationale: Is correct. defect density is related to the test object quality

options.text: Time needed to repair a defect
options.rationale: Is not correct. Time to repair is a process metric. It does not tell us anything about the product quality

stem.text: Which of the following pieces of information contained in a test progress report is the LEAST useful for business representatives?

options.text: Impediments to testing
options.rationale: Is not correct. Impediments to testing can be high-level and business- related, so this is an important piece of information for business stakeholders

options.text: Branch coverage achieved
options.rationale: Is correct. Branch testing is a technical metric used by developers and technical test analysts. This information is of no interest to business representatives

options.text: Test progress
options.rationale: Is not correct. Test progress is project related, so it may be useful for business representatives

options.text: New risks within the test cycle
options.rationale: Is not correct. Risks impact product quality, so it may be useful for business representatives
